text:
Mats Zuccarello's first season in Los Angeles has been mostly spent waiting. The Kings put him on injured reserve on Oct. 26 (after an earlier absence in October), and he returned Tuesday against Nashville. Eight games in, he has one assist, six shots and no goals.

At 39, is this rust or age? Eight scattered games can't say. The early five-on-five numbers are poor: the Kings have taken 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about eight points worse than without him. His ice time has dropped from 18 or 19 minutes in his first games to 11 and 13 in the two since he returned.

The case for patience is last season. Evolving-Hockey had him 73rd of 401 forwards by wins above replacement in Minnesota, mostly from even-strength offense, and he scored 54 points in 59 games. He has always been more passer than shooter, and that kind of player needs a linemate who can finish; a clip on the Kings' channel this week wondered if Kevin Fiala is the key.

Watch his minutes over the next two weeks. They will tell you how Los Angeles reads it.
